You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 3465bb1a1855be1ba4563ad839439e653ab5894e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ard Biesheuvel <ard.biesheuvel@linaro.org>
Date: Fri, 17 Jan 2020 12:16:51 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Silicon/SynQuacer/NetsecDxe: ignore DMA coherency at binding
 time

Whether the Netsec driver is built to support coherent or non-coherent
DMA is decided by the DmaLib library class resolution that is provided
by the platform description, and there are various other places where
the platform needs to be consistent with this (ACPI tables, device
tree, platform driver, etc)

Since the driver has no way to figure out which flavor of DmaLib it was
built against, there is no point in limiting it to one flavor only, and
we can drop the DmaType check at binding time entirely.

This fixes an issue introduced by commit 88c7874481b856578662b775
("Silicon/SynQuacer/PlatformDxe: set NETSEC DMA as coherent"), which
incorrectly stated that the driver does not look at the DmaType flag
in the first place.

Signed-off-by: Ard Biesheuvel <ard.biesheuvel@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Leif Lindholm <leif.lindholm@linaro.org>

diff --git a/Silicon/Socionext/SynQuacer/Drivers/Net/NetsecDxe/DriverBinding.c b/Silicon/Socionext/SynQuacer/Drivers/Net/NetsecDxe/DriverBinding.c
index 9820585e0d..392d1b474f 100644
--- a/Silicon/Socionext/SynQuacer/Drivers/Net/NetsecDxe/DriverBinding.c
+++ b/Silicon/Socionext/SynQuacer/Drivers/Net/NetsecDxe/DriverBinding.c
@@ -52,8 +52,7 @@ NetsecDriverBindingSupported (
     return Status;
   }
 
-  if (CompareGuid (Dev->Type, &gNetsecNonDiscoverableDeviceGuid) &&
-      Dev->DmaType == NonDiscoverableDeviceDmaTypeNonCoherent) {
+  if (CompareGuid (Dev->Type, &gNetsecNonDiscoverableDeviceGuid)) {
     Status = EFI_SUCCESS;
   } else {
     Status = EFI_UNSUPPORTED;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `DriverBinding.c`**
   - The conditional check for `Dev->DmaType` has been removed from the `NetsecDriverBindingSupported` function. 
   - The original check that limited the driver to only support non-coherent DMA for non-discoverable devices has been simplified to only check the device type against `gNetsecNonDiscoverableDeviceGuid`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `DriverBinding.c` addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit that incorrectly enforced a limitation on the DMA type during the driver binding process. By removing the `DmaType` check, the driver can now operate without being restricted to a specific DMA type, allowing it to function correctly regardless of whether it was built for coherent or non-coherent DMA. This change ensures consistency with the platform's DMA library configuration and resolves the issue caused by the earlier commit.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (CompareGuid (Dev->Type, &gNetsecNonDiscoverableDeviceGuid) &&
    Dev->DmaType == NonDiscoverableDeviceDmaTypeNonCoherent) {
```
Reason:
This code checks the `DmaType` of the non-discoverable device at binding time, which incorrectly restricts the driver to only support non-coherent DMA. This assumption conflicts with the platform's DMA library configuration, leading to compatibility issues since the driver cannot determine the correct DMA type it was built against.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (CompareGuid (Dev->Type, &gNetsecNonDiscoverableDeviceGuid)) {
```
Reason:
By removing the check for `Dev->DmaType`, the driver no longer limits its functionality based on the DMA type at binding time. This allows the driver to support both coherent and non-coherent DMA configurations, aligning it with the platform's DMA library settings and resolving the compatibility issues.
